cues: A wavefront is a surface of constant phase, and a ray is its normal.
Huygens' principle: every point on a wavefront sends out forward wavelets, and the new wavefront is their envelope.
Applied to a mirror, equal wavelets give i equals r. Applied to a denser medium, slower wavelets give sine i over sine r equals v one over v two, Snell's law.
The frequency never changes on refraction; the speed and wavelength fall by n, and the optical path is n x.
And Foucault's experiment settled it: light is a wave.
text: Let us recap. A wavefront is a surface of constant phase, and a ray is its normal. Huygens' principle: every point on a wavefront sends out forward wavelets, and the new wavefront is their envelope. Applied to a mirror, equal wavelets give i equals r. Applied to a denser medium, slower wavelets give sine i over sine r equals v one over v two, Snell's law. The frequency never changes on refraction; the speed and wavelength fall by n, and the optical path is n x. And Foucault's experiment settled it: light is a wave.
